EvidenceBody: Chan speakers use its cold, apparently lifeless condition as a test image, then make it do what such a tree cannot: grow branches, bloom, roar like a lion, or carry hidden news of warmth. Damei Fachang describes himself as a damaged dead tree unchanged by repeated springs; the hermit in the burned-hut case says a dead tree against a cold cliff has no warmth through three winters. Yunfeng Zudeng warns that treating cold ash and dead wood as the old masters' final position falls into a one-color understanding. The phrase therefore keeps the ordinary dead tree visible while public sayings test whether stillness has been mistaken for completion.
